title: Surjectivity of the actual residue tensor map for a finite-field constant extension
statement: Let k and F be finite fields and i:k\to F a field embedding. Let X be a finite-type k-scheme with structure f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Form Y=X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}F with projections p:Y\to X and q:Y\to\operatorname{Spec}F [def-pc-fibre-product, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let z be a closed point of Y and x=p(z). Write e:\kappa(x)\to\kappa(z) for the actual residue-field map of p and j:F\to\kappa(z) for the base-field residue embedding of q [def-weil-residue-field]. Their composites from k agree. The induced ring map \kappa(x)\otimes_k F\to\kappa(z) is surjective. Here the tensor is the commutative-ring pushout of the actual maps k\to\kappa(x) and i:k\to F, and the induced map is its universal map with restrictions e and j.

source.place: Tag 01JT, lemma-points-fibre-product, residue-field clause; direct finite-field universal-property proof by A8.

proof.text: The pullback is locally of finite type over F. By [lem-kun-closed-point-field], the closed point z has residue field K finite-dimensional over finite F, so K is a finite set. Let A be the image subring of the canonical tensor map into K. It is finite and is a domain. Multiplication by a nonzero element is injective and hence surjective, so A is a field. In Lean use Scheme.Hom.finite_residueField_of_isClosed, Module.finite_of_finite, and Finite.isField_of_domain.

source.place: Tag 01JT, lemma-points-fibre-product, residue-field clause; direct finite-field universal-property proof by A8.

proof.text: Both actual factor maps corestrict to A. By [lem-weil-pbc-residue-field-point-naturality], Spec of the first followed by the canonical point of x and Spec of the second form a compatible pair over Spec k. The displayed base-map equality is exactly this compatibility. The fibre-product universal property [def-pc-fibre-product] yields t:Spec A -> X_F. Composing with Spec of the inclusion A -> K gives the canonical point j_z:Spec K -> X_F, by equality of both projections.

source.place: Tag 01JT, lemma-points-fibre-product, residue-field clause; direct finite-field universal-property proof by A8.

proof.text: The unique point of Spec A maps to z. The field-valued-point bijection [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-from-spec-field] gives d:kappa(z) -> A with t=j_z composed with Spec(d). The equality after inclusion into K and uniqueness in that bijection give inclusion composed with d equal to the identity of K. Therefore every element of K belongs to A and has a tensor preimage.

theorem finiteFieldBaseChangeResidue_surjective
    {k F : Type u} [Field k] [Finite k] [Field F] [Finite F]
    (i : k →+* F) {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f]
    (z : ↥(pullback f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom i))))
    (hz : z ∈ closedPoints (↥(pullback f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom i)))))
    (h : CommRingCat.ofHom (f.residueFieldAlgebraMap
        (pullback.fst f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom i)) z)) ≫
        (pullback.fst f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom i))).residueFieldMap z =
      CommRingCat.ofHom i ≫ CommRingCat.ofHom
        ((pullback.snd f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom i))).residueFieldAlgebraMap z)) :
    Function.Surjective (pushout.desc
      ((pullback.fst f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom i))).residueFieldMap z)
      (CommRingCat.ofHom
        ((pullback.snd f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom i))).residueFieldAlgebraMap z)) h).hom
